policy.semantics: This layer documents one-sided mass violence and killings in which the victims could not mount an armed defence: entities Wikidata classes as massacre (Q3199915), plus two individually listed one-sided killings classed by Wikidata as a military operation or an airstrike, plus the police-raid class (Q97368680). It is deliberately NOT the battles layer: battles.json documents combat between opposing forces, and validate-atrocities.mjs fails if any entity id appears in both layers. The layer records the source classification only; it does not assert that a state, army or organised group was responsible for any incident, and it does not distinguish state, communal or criminal mass violence.
policy.language: Names are source labels, not editorial renderings. nameZh is taken, in this order, from a Chinese article found by search and confirmed to document the same event, the entity's Wikidata label in any Chinese variant (zh, zh-hans, zh-hant, zh-cn, zh-tw, zh-hk, zh-sg, zh-my), or the zh.wikipedia sitelink; it is quoted verbatim and may therefore be written in traditional script. When no Chinese source names the event nameZh is null. Nothing is transliterated or machine translated. nameEn is the Wikidata English label.
policy.coordinates: Points come from the Wikidata P625 statement of the incident entity; no coordinate is estimated or moved.
policy.dates: Years come from the P585 statement at single-year precision; no month or day is inferred. Wikidata stores ISO 8601 astronomical years, so BCE values are converted to the project civil-year convention, which has no year zero (ISO -489, i.e. 490 BCE, ships as -490).
policy.names: English names come from the Wikidata English label (293 of 302 pool records have one). Nine pool records carry neither a Chinese nor an English label and are not shipped; their count is recorded in counts.dropped.noName.
policy.countries: countriesZh, conflictZh and victimsZh repeat the Chinese labels recorded by the 3.15 sweep. The English arrays are resolved from the same Wikidata statements the Chinese labels came from: the entity's P17 (country), P361 (part of) and P710 (participant) values are read back, their Chinese labels are matched against the recorded strings, and the English label of that same entity is written in the matching slot. A slot whose statement entity could not be matched is null - it is never machine translated. counts.englishFieldCoverage records how many slots were resolved.
policy.provenance: Every entry links its Wikidata entity; statement-level reference URLs are included when Wikidata records them.
policy.coverage: The pool is the Wikidata sweep of the Oceania, South Asia and Southeast Asia coordinate boxes that build-battles.mjs excludes from the battle layer (editorial/battles-thin-regions-3.15.json). Chinese-name coverage is therefore a property of Wikidata, not of this build: see counts.withChineseName and counts.withoutChineseName.
policy.ui: No user interface consumes this layer in the 3.16 round. It ships as data plus the independent validator so a later round can decide how to present it, for example whether a Chinese-language mode shows only the sub-set with Chinese names.
policy.region: Regions are assigned by the documented coordinate box rule (regionBasis=coordinate-box), the same rule the battle layer uses.
policy.zhNamesRound: The 3.17 pass re-queried every Chinese label variant and the zh.wikipedia sitelink, then searched the Chinese Wikipedia by the English and Chinese names for the entities still without a name, reading each candidate introduction before accepting it; the confirmations and the rejected candidates are recorded in docs/verification-3.17/atrocities-zh-search.json and the round report.
